mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates expanding industrial production, reflecting stronger economic activity and higher earnings expectations, which drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.

failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS are cut by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month, it signals an aggressive easing cycle, lowering borrowing costs and boosting equity valuations through lower discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by >0.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mean return is not significantly above zero at 5% significance.
